title: What completeness buys
promptMarkdown: In your own words, and without the notes open, explain in under 200 words why completeness of a normed space matters when one solves problems by approximation. Then give one concrete example of a sequence that is Cauchy in a normed space but whose limit lies outside that space (you may use the example from exercise 2 or another).
hintLadder: What do iterative or approximation methods produce? A sequence. What do you need to know about that sequence to say the method 'converges to a solution'?
Compare $\mathbb{Q}$ and $\mathbb{R}$: which Cauchy sequences of rationals have no rational limit?

criteria.criterion: Explains that approximation schemes produce Cauchy sequences whose limits must exist inside the space for the scheme to yield a solution there.

levels.label: not met
levels.description: Missing or confused with boundedness or closedness.

criteria.criterion: Gives a correct concrete example of a Cauchy sequence without a limit in the space.

levels.label: met
levels.description: Example correct and the missing limit identified.

difficulty.basis: A short explanation of one idea (approximation schemes produce Cauchy sequences whose limits must lie in the space) and one example, which exercise 2 or the rationals can supply.
